name: Constitutional Megaloblastic Anemia Due to Folate Metabolism Disorder
aliases: Congenital Megaloblastic Anemia Related to Folate Pathway

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Megaloblastic Anemia Due to Folate Metabolism Disorder

criteria.description: Presence of macrocytic anemia with elevated mean corpuscular volume (MCV)
Low serum folate levels confirmed by biochemical assays
Bone marrow examination showing megaloblastic changes with nuclear-cytoplasmic asynchrony
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in folate metabolism

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of macrocytic anemia with low serum folate and bone marrow megaloblastosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and response to folate supplementation support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

searchTerms: large red blood cells with abnormal neutrophils
macrocytic anemia with hypersegmented white cells
enlarged red cells and abnormal neutrophils
abnormal large red blood cell precursors in marrow
defective red cell development in marrow
tongue soreness with loss of bumps

common.symptomName: Dyspnea on exertion due to anemia
Mild jaundice secondary to ineffective erythropoiesis
searchTerms: mild jaundice from poor red cell production
slight yellowing due to ineffective erythropoiesis

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to severe anemia
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems due to low blood count

rare.symptomName: Recurrent infections due to immunological impairment
searchTerms: recurrent infections due to immune problems

rare.symptomName: Ophthalmological changes such as optic neuropathy

laboratory: Low serum and red blood cell folate concentrations
Normal or low vitamin B12 levels
imaging: Generally unremarkable; imaging may be used to exclude other causes
genetic: Mutations in genes encoding enzymes of folate metabolism such as MTHFR, DHFR, or FOLR1
other: Positive response to folate supplementation with hematological improvement

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of low vitamin B12 levels
Neurological symptoms more prominent and frequent
Positive intrinsic factor antibody in pernicious anemia
Dysplastic changes in multiple hematopoietic lineages
Cytogenetic abnormalities on bone marrow analysis
Lack of response to folate supplementation

redFlags: Severe pancytopenia with bleeding or infection
Failure to respond to folate supplementation
references: Orphanet: Constitutional Megaloblastic Anemia Due to Folate Metabolism Disorder (ORPHA:98408)
